entries.why: the constructor's options gained an optional seed (ReleaseSeed | null)
the instance gained seedAtStart (SeedAnswer | null) and the private #seed and #loadReleaseSeed
its options gained an optional seed
it hands back an AiCatalogue, whose instance gained seedAtStart and private members
gained the optional AI_CATALOGUE_SEED_SIGNATURE and AI_CATALOGUE_DEVELOPMENT, with a bound line on the latter

notes: The behaviour that matters most is not in the listing: start() now loads the release's seed (it writes a payload row and a seed becomes the current payload at boot), and the trusted keys are now filtered by the environment (a development key line is refused unless AI_CATALOGUE_DEVELOPMENT is "1"). A user that counted on an empty catalogue at boot, or on development keys being trusted, sees no kind change for it; only the new optional env members and the instance's new member show. The instance's hands-back change comes partly from private members (#seed, #loadReleaseSeed), which the tool lists; I expect it to report AiCatalogue and aiCatalogueOf as handing back differently because of them, which is a notice for nothing for users that only call methods.

Only seed.mjs's header comment changed (CATALOGUE_KEYS now holds Bob's two keys alone, in signatures), and a test was added confirming it. No interface comment needed to change. The real change is in signatures' CATALOGUE_KEYS, which this module uses as the constructor's default keys; that default's value is content, not a kind, so the listing of ai-catalogue does not move.

entries.why: lines may now be null or undefined (Bob's lines alone); env gained the optional AI_CATALOGUE_DEVELOPMENT_KEY
gained the optional AI_CATALOGUE_DEVELOPMENT_KEY (unknown) with a bound line
its options' env (CatalogueEnv, written out in full) gained an optional member
its options' env gained an optional member

notes: The new member arrives with a bound line (AI_CATALOGUE_DEVELOPMENT_KEY: one ssh-ed25519 line marked -development, trusted only where AI_CATALOGUE_DEVELOPMENT is "1"); the tool attaches nested bounds to every entry whose kind reaches CatalogueEnv (CatalogueEnv, AiCatalogue, aiCatalogueOf, catalogueKeysFor), so it may report 'bound changed' on those four rather than only 'accepts more'. By the method the bound belongs to a member that did not exist, so nothing accepted before is refused. Behaviour not in the listing: in a development build, catalogueKeysFor now adds the deployment's own key line, and a caller passing no list now gets Bob's lines rather than an empty list. The new file dev-key.mjs is a command, not an interface file (not public, not re-exported); I gave it the start kinds rule 34 asks for (DevKeyArgv @message argv, DevKeyEnv @message env) with casts on each process.argv and process.env read; they are not in the listing.

Only dev-key.mjs changed: a new exported constant GUARD_LINE, and CF_TOKEN is now required in a dry run too (the Worker is looked up before the key is made). dev-key.mjs is not an interface file (modules.json public is src/checks.mjs and src/index.mjs, and index.mjs does not re-export it), so the listing does not move. I changed one bound line on DevKeyEnv (@message env) for the token; that kind is in a non-public file, so the tool should not list it. If the tool treats a start kind (@message env) as published wherever it is written, it would see 'bound changed' on DevKeyEnv; its users are the process's deploy step, outside the product.

entries.why: re-exported from seed.mjs; its kind is the reader's inference, not CataloguePayload

notes: No existing entry's kind changes: the constructor's seed option keeps its kind (ReleaseSeed | null), only its default moves (with no seed given, a development build now loads DEVELOPMENT_SEED, which lists a plan and an entry, instead of the empty RELEASE_SEED). That is behaviour the listing does not carry; a user (ai-accounts, ai-use) on a development plane now sees a catalogue with a plan where it saw none. dev-key.mjs (not an interface file) now signs DEVELOPMENT_SEED. I could not give DEVELOPMENT_SEED_PAYLOAD the kind CataloguePayload without typing seed.mjs's eight builder helpers (a cast was refused by rule 14 because the helpers' answers widen), so its listed kind is the reader's inference; a later change inside it would show as 'hands back differently' on a constant.

Behaviour not in the listing: in a development build whose development seed verifies, start() now registers DEVELOPMENT_ADAPTERS itself, so the seed's entry no longer needs a newer release and entriesFor offers it. No kind of an existing entry changes (registerAdapterTypes is called from inside; #loadReleaseSeed's answer is unchanged).

entries.why: the instance gained the methods catalogueRead and resultsRead and the private #listingOf
it hands back an AiCatalogue, which gained two methods and a private one
the screens' read of the whole catalogue
the screens' read of the results library
the handlers of the module's two operations

notes: The two new operation names (aicatalogueread, airesultsread) are new to the product as far as I can see; if another module already answers either name, rule 7 tells that operation's users. The change also moves CATALOGUE_ADDRESS from .../catalogue/index.json to .../ai/index.json, so every payload path now resolves under /ai/. That is a real change in the contract with ai-issuer, which must serve there, and with anyone reading pullRequest's url. But the constant is a lone string, which the tool lists as `string`, and my bound line on PullRequestAnswer.url names the constant rather than its value, so I expect no listing change and no notice for it (a possible miss, if ai-issuer was not already serving /ai/). The class's hands-back change shows partly through the private #listingOf.
